content: What is the change in transparency for theorems?

lean4#14896: Theorems should be like opaque. I actually intended to make that change in March (lean4#12973) but screwed up and nobody noticed and told me until very recently. So now I am folding this change into the Kernel Renovations (lean4#14977).

But con-leche applies a trick: In practice (e.g. stuff produced by the elaborator) we eliminated virtually all places where theorems have to be unfolded. Only large elimination of And.rec remains. If you add k-like treatment to that (i.e. always reduce without reducing the subject, passing projections to the minor premise), it work as well.

Once the renovation is done this little sneaky trick can be dropped, of course.
Wait sorry, why would a theorem ever be unfolded in the first place, with proof irrelevance?

You'd think that, wouldn't you? I certainly did back then :-)
I believe it was mainly to reduce proofs of Acc in well founded definitions. But it caused plenty of problems (mostly practical, but also theoretical, non-transitivity of defeq), so we want to get rid of it.
